function.name: pwsh
function.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry. Raise it for installs and downloads.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

function.name: read
function.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

function.name: write
function.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact file operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact file operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

function.name: read_image
function.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

function.name: glob
function.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matching-line previews within 20480 bytes; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

function.name: skill
function.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web for sources, including papers and preprints, returning available text and URLs. Use site to search a specific website.

query.description: Concise topic, exact entity names and necessary context; at most 200 characters.

location.description: Defaults to cn for China-focused sources. Use global for broader or English-language sources, or when cn results are insufficient. Query language does not select the source pool.

site.description: Limit to this bare domain and its subdomains, e.g. arxiv.org or nature.com. Omit or leave empty for unrestricted search.

recency.description: Prefer sources from this recent period; defaults to noLimit. Verify critical publication dates.

numResults.description: Maximum results, 1–10; defaults to 5. Use fewer for focused questions. Filtering may yield fewer.

function.name: web_fetch
function.description: Read known web pages or PDFs. Saves extracted content for read and grep. For arXiv full text, use the corresponding /pdf URL.

urls.description: 1–100 absolute HTTP(S) URLs without embedded credentials. Batch useful URLs together; duplicates are read once.

function.name: paper_search
function.description: Look up paper records in a literature index. Returns title, authors, journal, publication date, DOI, and abstract when available. Supports publication-date bounds and a Chinese-language corpus.

query.description: Paper title or specific keywords for the work you need the record of.

language.description: Paper corpus: zh for Chinese, en for English (default); independent of the answer language.

startPublishedDate.description: Inclusive lower bound, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC) or ISO timestamp with timezone. Missing or incomplete source dates are excluded.

endPublishedDate.description: Inclusive upper bound in the same format; a date includes the whole UTC day.

numResults.description: Maximum results, 1–10; defaults to 5. Use fewer for focused questions. Filtering may yield fewer.

function.name: generate_image
function.description: Generate a new image from a prompt, or edit or combine up to five existing images by path. Saves a PNG or JPEG file in the workspace and returns its path.

prompt.description: Complete description of the image: subject, style or medium, composition and viewpoint, colors and lighting, the aspect ratio in words, and any text to render, quoted exactly. When editing, describe what to change and what to keep.

reference_images.description: Edit mode: paths of up to 5 images to modify or use as references, resolved by the filesystem backend like read_image. Omit to generate from the prompt alone.

detail.description: How much fine detail the image needs; default standard. standard: most images, single subjects, simple compositions, drafts, iterations, quick previews. fine: many small elements, any Chinese text, dense text that must be exactly right, edits that must preserve the reference's details, or an explicitly requested polished result; more than twice as slow and more expensive.

file_path.description: Where to save the image, resolved by the filesystem backend like write; the extension selects the format, .png or .jpg/.jpeg. Omit to save a PNG under generated_images/ in the workspace.

function.name: memory_write
function.description: Immediately save, revise, or forget a memory explicitly requested by the current user. Read an existing record block in the handbook to obtain its id and version before revising or forgetting.

evidence.description: Exact quote from the current user message.

id.description: Existing memory id for update or forget.

expectedVersion.description: Version read from the existing handbook record block.

key.description: Stable semantic key, such as answer_length or professional_role.

function.name: ask_user_question
function.description: Ask brief, direct, self-contained questions about missing information, preferences, or decisions. Use user-facing terms; assume no knowledge of background work or internal names. Use distinct stable question IDs. A submitted skipped question is an answer item with empty selected and no custom; pending instead means no answer batch arrived before the timeout and the user can still answer.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user; the UI always adds its own free-text "Other" field, so every option should be a concrete answer. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

function.name: subagent
function.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. This call waits for the subagent to finish and returns its final report, not its intermediate steps. The subagent inherits your model and working directory and cannot ask the user anything.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

function.name: browser
function.description: Operate the browser: open/read pages, click/type/scroll, reload, wait, inspect layout, diagnostics and screenshots. Only supply fields needed by the action. Ref actions require the current pageVersion from read. Screenshot returns a persisted PNG and, on image-capable models, image content.

tabId.description: Target tab returned by the browser. Omit to use current tab.

keys.description: send_keys: e.g. Enter, Tab, Escape, ArrowDown.

width.description: set_viewport ONLY. Never supply to screenshot; use clip for cropping.

height.description: set_viewport ONLY. Never supply to screenshot.
